Slice: Overdue Loans To Notify

Intent

The list of overdue loans whose borrowers have not yet been sent an overdue notice. The overdue notice gateway works through it, so each borrower with an overdue loan is emailed once, as soon as the loan is overdue. Each item carries everything the email needs, so the gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Overdue Notice Gateway, a system reaction in the Send Overdue Notice slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the gateway does with it: for each loan on the list, it hands one notice to the email provider and records Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice slice). How often it checks the list is that slice's concern.

Read Model / View

  • View: Overdue Loans To Notify built from events: "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Overdue Notice Gateway (Send Overdue Notice). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a loan is overdue is worked out when the list is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so a loan is on the list from the first read after midnight following its due date.

The view keeps one row for every open loan that hasn't been sent a notice; the query returns only the overdue ones. LoanId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId Tool Checked Out.loanId.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Tool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
dueDate Date Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
toolName Text Tool Checked Out.toolName.
borrowerName Text Tool Checked Out.neighborName.
borrowerEmail Text Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborEmail, replaced by each later Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor. Always the current one.
overdue Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-OLN-1). Worked out when the list is read.

A row carries everything it needs from its own Tool Checked Out; the view keeps no bookkeeping beyond its rows. Neighbor Email Changed updates the address on that neighbor's rows only.

When a row leaves the view. A loan's row is removed when Overdue Notice Sent, Tool Returned or Tool Lost is recorded for it (INV-OLN-8). Nothing puts it back.

Queries

  • List loans to notify. Takes nothing. Returns every row whose overdue is yes, with loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the gateway, which sends one notice per loan.

Invariants / Business Rules

A loan is ready for its notice as soon as it joins the list. When the email goes out, with no quiet hours, is Send Overdue Notice's rule (INV-OVN-6, Send Overdue Notice).

  • INV-OLN-1: A loan is on the list from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while the tool is still out and no overdue notice has been sent for it.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue; the loan joins the list because the date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-2: A loan's due date is the one set at checkout, moved by each extension.
    • A loan extended before it became overdue joins the list only once its new due date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-3: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, the loan leaves the list and never comes back.
    • One notice per loan. An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so it stays overdue until it ends, and no second notice goes out.
  • INV-OLN-4: When the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost, its loan leaves the list.
    • A loan that ends this way before its notice went out never gets a notice.
    • A closed account never has a loan on the list, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
    • A loan whose tool is retired while it is out stays on the list and still gets its notice: the loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-OLN-6: Each loan on the list carries everything the notice needs: the borrower's name and email, the tool's name, and the due date.
    • The borrower's name and email come with Tool Checked Out, and the email is kept current: a later Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The tool's name and the due date come from Tool Checked Out, the due date moved by any Loan Extended. The gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.
  • INV-OLN-8: A loan leaves the list only when an overdue notice is sent for it, when the tool is returned, or when the tool is recorded lost.
    • A notice that later fails to deliver doesn't put the loan back on the list. The failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and no further attempt is made.
  • INV-OLN-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Loan not yet overdue (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: Ana (N1) borrowing the cordless drill (T1), due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not returned.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-OLN-1, INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1, Ana Ruiz's (N1, ana@example.org) loan of T1 "Cordless drill", is due 12 October, still out
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is returned, with toolName "Cordless drill", borrowerName "Ana Ruiz", borrowerEmail ana@example.org, and dueDate 12 October.
  • Extended before it became overdue (INV-OLN-2)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1 on 10 October, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: L1 is not returned when the list is read on 13 October, and is returned from 00:00 on 20 October if still out.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-8)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and is never returned again while the drill is out.
  • Returned before the notice (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 before any notice is sent
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and still out, and Tool Retired was recorded for T1 on 11 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned, ready for its notice.
  • Borrower changes their email (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is on the list, carrying ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • Then: L1 stays on the list, now carrying ana@example.org, so the notice goes to the new address.
  • Email changed before the loan is overdue (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October, and N1's email was changed to ana@example.org on 10 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned carrying ana@example.org.
  • Several borrowers (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: L1 (Ana, due 12 October) and L2 (Ben, due 14 October) are both out
    • When: the list is read on 13 October
    • Then: only L1 is returned.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: L1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still on the list once.
  • Replayed sent notice (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, so L1 is off the list
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Sent is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still off the list.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-OLN-9). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has left the list: once a loan's row is removed, a later Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost for it (a replay) changes nothing. An Overdue Notice Failed doesn't reach this list at all.
  • The gateway reads a loan twice before Overdue Notice Sent lands: the list may return the same loan on two reads in a row. Sending one notice per loan is the Send Overdue Notice slice's rule, enforced when it records Overdue Notice Sent; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Overdue Notice Gateway. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and hands them to the gateway only for borrowers with an overdue loan. It shows them on no screen.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. A loan is ready as soon as it joins the list; how soon the email goes out after that is Send Overdue Notice's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, toolName, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/extend-loan.md and slices/my-loans.md. Change Email, Send Overdue Notice, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Send Overdue Notice, whose gateway works from this list and records Overdue Notice Sent.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Neighbors To Flag

Intent

The late-return flagger's to-do list: every neighbor whose late returns have reached the threshold (3 within 90 days) and who hasn't yet been flagged for them, with the loans those late returns belong to, each with the tool's name, the due date it missed and the date it came back. The flagger works through it, so the shed manager sees each of these neighbors flagged on Neighbors and decides whether to suspend them.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Late Return Flagger, a system processor in the Flag Neighbor slice (slices/flag-neighbor.md). No person or screen reads this list.
  • What the flagger does with it: for each neighbor returned, it issues Flag Neighbor naming the loans returned, which the flag uses up.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors To Flag built from events: "Tool Returned", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Late Return Flagger (Flag Neighbor). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events (seconds, not minutes). Which late returns are still within the 90 days is worked out when the list is read, from returnedOn and today's date in the shed's local time zone.

The view keeps one row for every late return that can still count toward a flag; the query groups them by neighbor. LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Tool Returned.neighborId: the borrower.
loanId LoanId Tool Returned.loanId.
toolName Text Tool Returned.toolName. Carried onto the flag.
dueDate Date Tool Returned.dueDate: the due date in force at the return. Carried onto the flag.
returnedOn Date Tool Returned.returnedOn.
inWindow Bool Derived: yes while returnedOn is today or one of the 89 days before it, in the shed's local time zone (INV-NTF-2). Worked out when the list is read.

To decide whether a return creates a row, the view also keeps, beyond its rows, every neighbor's current status: active, suspended (from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated) or closed (from Neighbor Account Closed). This is bookkeeping, not rows, and is never returned.

When a row is created. Tool Returned with late = yes creates a row for the loan's borrower, unless the borrower is suspended or their account is closed (INV-NTF-6, INV-NTF-7). An on-time return creates nothing. Lateness is read from Tool Returned.late, recorded once by Return Tool; this view never works it out.

When rows are removed.

  • Neighbor Flagged removes the rows for the loans it names as used up (INV-NTF-3).
  • Neighbor Suspended and Neighbor Reinstated remove all of the neighbor's rows (INV-NTF-5, INV-NTF-7).
  • Neighbor Account Closed removes all of the neighbor's rows (INV-NTF-6).

Nothing puts a row back.

Queries

  • List neighbors to flag. Takes nothing. Returns each neighbor who has at least 3 rows with inWindow yes, with their neighborId and those rows as late returns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn; all of them, if more than 3). There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the flagger.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NTF-1: Only late returns count toward the threshold.
    • Whether a return was late is recorded on Tool Returned (late), worked out by Return Tool against the loan's due date in force, after any extensions. A return on the due date is on time.
    • A loan that is still out doesn't count, even if it is overdue, until it is returned late.
    • A tool recorded lost never counts as a late return, even if the loan was overdue: it is never returned, so it never produces a Tool Returned.
  • INV-NTF-2: A neighbor is on the list when they have 3 or more late returns within the last 90 days that haven't counted toward a flag.
    • The 90 days are a rolling window, counted back from today by the date of each return. A late return older than that no longer counts. A late return counts on the day it was returned and the next 89 days, 90 calendar days in all, in the shed's local time. A return on 1 June counts through 29 August.
  • INV-NTF-3: Once Neighbor Flagged is recorded for a neighbor, the late returns it names are used up and never count again.
    • Neighbor Flagged carries every late return that counted when the flag was recorded. This list uses them up by loan; Neighbors shows them.
    • The neighbor leaves the list, and is flagged again only after 3 new late returns within 90 days.
    • A flag the shed manager doesn't act on stays open on Neighbors. It doesn't put the neighbor back on this list.
  • INV-NTF-5: Reinstatement starts a neighbor's late-return count again from zero.
    • Late returns from before Neighbor Reinstated never count toward a later flag.
  • INV-NTF-6: A neighbor whose account is closed is never flagged.
    • Once Neighbor Account Closed is recorded, the neighbor leaves the list if they are on it. An account can't be closed while tools are on loan, so no late return follows a closure.
  • INV-NTF-7: A suspended neighbor is never flagged.
    • Once Neighbor Suspended is recorded, the neighbor leaves the list if they are on it, and late returns while they are suspended aren't counted. Reinstatement then starts their count again from zero.
  • INV-NTF-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The list has no screen; only the Late Return Flagger reads it. The shed manager sees flagged neighbors on Neighbors.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana is an active neighbor with no late returns counting, and today is 5 October.

  • On-time return doesn't count (INV-NTF-1)
    • Given: Ana's drill loan L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 on 12 October, with late = no
    • Then: no row is created, and Ana is not on the list.
  • Late return below the threshold (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has one late return counting, on 1 September
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L2 on 20 September, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has two late returns counting, and she is not on the list.
  • Third late return within 90 days (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1 September (L1) and 20 September (L2)
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L3 on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: the list returns Ana with L1, L2 and L3.
  • Old late return has dropped out of the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns on 1 June and 20 September, neither used up
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: only two of Ana's late returns are within 90 days, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Four late returns in the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1, 10 and 20 September, and the flagger hasn't acted yet
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: the list returns Ana with all four loans.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NTF-3)
    • Given: the list returns Ana with L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: those rows are removed, and Ana is not on the list.
  • Flagged again only on new late returns (INV-NTF-3)
    • Given: Ana was flagged on 5 October, using up L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L4 on 12 October, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has one late return counting, L4, and she is not on the list.
  • Reinstatement resets the count (INV-NTF-5)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has since been reinstated, and had two late returns counting before her suspension
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 10 October, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has one late return counting, and she is not on the list.
  • Account closed while on the list (INV-NTF-6)
    • Given: the list returns Ana, waiting to be flagged
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana's rows are removed, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Suspended while on the list (INV-NTF-7)
    • Given: the list returns Ana, waiting to be flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana's rows are removed, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Late return while suspended (INV-NTF-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan, with late = yes
    • Then: no row is created.
  • Last day in the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 8 July, 20 September and 1 October; today is 5 October, which is 89 days after 8 July
    • When: the list is read on 5 October
    • Then: all three are in the window, and the list returns Ana.
  • First day out of the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: as above, but today is 6 October, 90 days after 8 July
    • When: the list is read on 6 October
    • Then: the 8 July return no longer counts, and the list doesn't return Ana.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NTF-8)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1 and 20 September
    • When: the same Tool Returned for her 20 September return is applied again
    • Then: Ana still has two late returns counting.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NTF-8).
  • The flagger reads a neighbor twice before Neighbor Flagged lands: the list may return the same neighbor on two reads in a row. Flagging once for the same late returns is Flag Neighbor's rule, enforced when it records Neighbor Flagged; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Late Return Flagger. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds neighbor and loan IDs and return dates only. No names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, neighborId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn, late.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, lateReturns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn): the late returns it uses up.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match return-tool.md. Loan Extended is no longer read here: lateness comes from Tool Returned.late.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Late Return Flagger reads it and issues Flag Neighbor.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded to Neighbors (2026-11-01)

Slice: Retire Tool

Intent

Take a tool out of the shed for good: a damaged tool, one the shed no longer keeps, or one added with a mistake. The shed manager retires it from Tool Inventory, and neighbors can no longer borrow or hold it. Retiring is final: nothing un-retires a tool. A tool retired to correct a mistake in its details is added again as a new tool.

What follows a retirement is decided by the views and slices that read Tool Retired:

  • The tool drops off the Tool Catalog at once (INV-TCAT-8). It drops off Tool Inventory at once if it is in the shed. A tool retired while on loan stays on Tool Inventory, shown as retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost (INV-TINV-2), so the shed manager can still record it lost if it never comes back.
  • Every hold on the tool ends, waiting or set aside: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for each in the same decision. No hold is passed on, and the holders are not told; their holds drop off My Holds (INV-MYHD-7).
  • A loan on the tool carries on, can't be extended (INV-EXT-8), and ends when the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • Check Out Tool and Place Hold refuse a retired tool.

A tool lost or broken by a borrower, and never returned, is not retired here. The shed manager records it lost against the loan (Record Tool Lost), which ends the loan and retires the tool in one step. A lost tool that later turns up is added again as a new tool.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Inventory screen, which offers Retire on every listed tool not already retired (INV-TINV-7). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role.

Command / Input

Command: Retire Tool

A ToolId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
toolId ToolId yes The tool to retire. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-RTR-10). It may be in the shed, on loan, reserved or set aside (INV-RTR-6).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Inventory @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Retired → context Tools Read by: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is retired) and My Loans (a loan on it is marked).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
toolId ToolId yes From the command.
retiredAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

Nothing is recorded about the tool's condition or the reason it was retired: the event carries no reason, note or condition. A damaged tool is the shed manager's call to retire.

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices, as any cancellation (the hold ends).

The same event Cancel Hold records, recorded here once per hold on the tool, waiting or set aside, in the same decision as Tool Retired. The decider reads the holds it ends. With no such hold, none is recorded; the readers can't tell these from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes Set by the system: the hold being ended, from its Hold Placed.
cancelledAt Instant yes Set by the system: the same moment as Tool Retired.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Retired changes the tool's entry in Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog and marks a loan on it in My Loans; the Hold Cancelled recorded with it end its holds in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-RTR-1: Only the shed manager can retire a tool.
    • Neighbors do not retire tools. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused with not-shed-manager.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-RTR-2: Retiring a tool that is already retired records nothing new.
    • The request succeeds, so a double submit or a retry never fails and never records a second Tool Retired. This includes a tool retired by being recorded lost.
  • INV-RTR-6: A tool can be retired whatever its state: in the shed, on loan, reserved or set aside.
    • Retiring is never refused because of a loan or a hold.
  • INV-RTR-10: The tool must exist.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: the ladder is in the shed, available, with no holds on it
    • When: the shed manager retires the ladder from Tool Inventory
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder, and nothing else.
  • Tool set aside, another hold waiting (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: the cordless drill is set aside for Ben, and Cara's hold on it is waiting
    • When: the shed manager retires the drill
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill, and Hold Cancelled for Ben's hold and for Cara's.
  • Tool on loan, with a hold waiting (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: Ana has the hedge trimmer on loan, due 20 October, and Ben's hold on it is waiting
    • When: the shed manager retires the hedge trimmer
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer, and Hold Cancelled for Ben's hold. Ana's loan is unchanged.
  • Tool reserved (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned with Ben's hold waiting, and Hold Fulfilled hasn't been recorded yet
    • When: the shed manager retires the drill
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill, and Hold Cancelled for Ben's hold.
  • Retiring twice (INV-RTR-2)
    • Given: Tool Retired has been recorded for the ladder
    • When: the shed manager retires the ladder again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Retiring a tool recorded lost (INV-RTR-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for Ana's loan of the hedge trimmer, which retired it
    • When: the shed manager retires the hedge trimmer
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-RTR-1)
    • Given: the ladder is in the shed
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to retire it
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can retire tools." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-RTR-10)
    • Given: no tool T9 has been added
    • When: the shed manager retires T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-RTR-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to retire the ladder
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Inventory screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then not-shed-manager (INV-RTR-1).
  2. tool-not-found (INV-RTR-10).
  3. If the tool is already retired, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-RTR-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-RTR-1
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can retire tools. INV-RTR-1
tool-not-found There is no such tool. INV-RTR-10

not-shed-manager and tool-not-found mean the same conditions as in Add Tool and Check Out Tool. tool-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: retiring a tool that is already retired succeeds and records nothing (INV-RTR-2).

Requests at the same moment: Retire Tool is decided against the tool's events as already recorded, one at a time per tool. If a checkout, a hold or a fulfilment for the tool is decided just before the retirement, it stands, and the retirement then ends the loan's chance of extension and the tool's holds. If it is decided just after, it is refused by its own slice because the tool is retired.

There are no external calls in this slice, and no email is sent.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may retire a tool (INV-RTR-1). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role.
  • PII & compliance: none. Tool Retired holds only the tool and a time.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Retired (this slice): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId (a lost tool is retired by that).
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs and the loan-ending convention.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog and My Loans (Tool Retired); My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire and Pickup Notices To Send (the Hold Cancelled recorded here). Check Out Tool, Place Hold, Extend Loan and Fulfill Hold read whether a tool is retired.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Record Tool Lost

Intent

Let the shed manager record that a tool out on loan is lost or broken and won't come back. Doing so ends the loan, so the borrower isn't left blocked by a tool they can't return, and takes the tool out of the shed for good, ending any holds on it.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Inventory screen, on a tool shown as out on loan ("mark lost", INV-TINV-6). That includes a tool retired while out. The borrower doesn't record a loss, and the shed manager doesn't record a return on the borrower's behalf instead.

Command / Input

Command: Record Tool Lost

A LoanId and a ToolId are UUIDs.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes The loan the tool is out on, as Tool Inventory shows it. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-LOST-11) and is still out (INV-LOST-2).
toolId ToolId yes The tool, as Tool Inventory shows it: the request is made at the tool's address (constitution Amendment 10, tools sit under /api/tools/{toolId}). Must be the loan's own tool (INV-LOST-11).

There is no field for cost, replacement, or what happened: nothing about it is recorded. A replacement, or the same tool if it turns up later, is added again as a new tool (Add Tool); the lost tool itself stays retired. The command carries no "from" value: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Inventory @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Lost → context Tools Read by: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool drops off), My Loans (the loan drops off), Overdue Loans To Notify (the loan leaves the list) and Undelivered Notices (an overdue-notice entry for the loan drops off).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes The loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out (the same as the command's, by INV-LOST-11). Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
lostAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. Tool Lost carries two of its three consequences: the loan ends and the tool is retired; every reader treats it as Tool Retired and no separate Tool Retired is recorded. The third, every hold on the tool ending, is recorded as its own facts:

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices, as any cancellation (the hold ends).

The same event Cancel Hold records, recorded here once per hold on the tool, in the same decision as Tool Lost. The decider reads the holds it ends. With no such hold, none is recorded; the readers can't tell these from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes Set by the system: the hold being ended, from its Hold Placed.
cancelledAt Instant yes Set by the system: the same moment as Tool Lost.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Lost updates Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; the Hold Cancelled recorded with it end the tool's holds in My Holds and the hold to-do lists. Each is specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

A lost tool never counts as a late return, even if its loan was overdue: Tool Lost isn't a Tool Returned, and only late returns count toward a flag (Neighbors To Flag; Flag Neighbor).

Tool Lost has three consequences, each owned by the slices that read it. The loan ends: after Tool Lost it can't be returned (INV-RET-2, Return Tool) or extended (Extend Loan), and it is no longer out. The tool is retired: it can't be borrowed (Check Out Tool), held (INV-HOLD-3, Place Hold) or retired again (Retire Tool), and every reader treats it as Tool Retired. Every hold on the tool ends (My Holds, Holds To Fulfill). An overdue loan ended this way no longer blocks the borrower's checkouts and pickups (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-5, counts only open loans), and no overdue notice goes out for it afterwards (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). The borrower isn't emailed; the loan simply drops off their My Loans. Holders aren't told their hold ended, as for any retired tool.

  • INV-LOST-1: Only the shed manager records a tool lost.
    • Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • INV-LOST-2: A tool can be recorded lost only while it is out on loan, and the loss is recorded against that loan.
    • It can be recorded at any time while the tool is out, before or after the loan is overdue.
    • A tool retired while out on loan can still be recorded lost.
    • A loan that has been returned can't be recorded lost.
  • INV-LOST-3: Recording a tool lost records Tool Lost and, for each hold on the tool, Hold Cancelled; nothing else.
    • No Tool Returned or Tool Retired is recorded: Tool Lost itself ends the loan and retires the tool. The holds end as Holds facts, so the views about holds hear only their own events.
  • INV-LOST-10: Recording a loan lost that is already recorded lost succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second loss.
  • INV-LOST-11: The loan must have been checked out, and the request must name the loan's own tool.
    • A request at a tool's address for a loan that is not that tool's loan names no loan there, and is refused loan-not-found like an unknown loan. The two are not told apart.
  • INV-LOST-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-LOST-1, INV-LOST-2, INV-LOST-3)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, due 12 October, and it is overdue. Ben's hold H1 on T2 is waiting.
    • When: on 20 October the shed manager records L2 lost from Tool Inventory
    • Then: Tool Lost is recorded for L2, with toolId T2 and the time it was recorded, and Hold Cancelled for H1. No Tool Returned or Tool Retired is recorded: Tool Lost ends L2 and retires T2.
  • Lost before the due date (INV-LOST-2)
    • Given: Ana has the hedge trimmer (T3) on loan L3, due 25 October, and it is 15 October
    • When: the shed manager records L3 lost
    • Then: Tool Lost is recorded for L3, with toolId T3.
  • Lost after being retired while out (INV-LOST-2)
    • Given: Tool Retired was recorded for the drill (T1) while Ben had it on loan L4
    • When: the shed manager records L4 lost from Tool Inventory
    • Then: Tool Lost is recorded for L4, with toolId T1.
  • Recorded lost twice (INV-LOST-10)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for L2
    • When: the same Record Tool Lost request for L2 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Already returned (INV-LOST-2)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L5
    • When: the shed manager tries to record L5 lost
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-LOST-1)
    • Given: Ana has L2 out
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to record L2 lost
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can record tools lost." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-LOST-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: the shed manager asks to record L9 lost
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Wrong tool for the loan (INV-LOST-11)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2
    • When: the shed manager asks to record L2 lost at the hedge trimmer's (T3) address
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-LOST-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for recording a tool lost arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Inventory screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-LOST-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-LOST-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. loan-not-found (INV-LOST-11).
  4. If Tool Lost is already recorded for the loan, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-LOST-10).
  5. loan-ended, if Tool Returned is recorded for the loan (INV-LOST-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-LOST-12
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can record tools lost. INV-LOST-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-LOST-11
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-LOST-2

The names mean the same conditions as in Add Tool, Suspend Neighbor, Return Tool and Extend Loan. loan-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen, which offers "mark lost" only on a tool shown as out, at that tool's address. A missing or malformed loan ID or tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a loss is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was recorded lost succeeds and records nothing. A loan that was returned is refused, because recording it lost would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: Record Tool Lost is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a loss and a return for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (the return then gets loan-ended; the loss gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a loss).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may record a tool lost (INV-LOST-1). Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Lost names a loan and a tool. It holds no name or email, and nothing about cost or blame.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (this slice): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/return-tool.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (Tool Lost); My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists (the Hold Cancelled recorded here). Return Tool and Extend Loan refuse the ended loan; Check Out Tool, Place Hold and Retire Tool treat the tool as retired.

Open Questions

  • Declare toolId on Record Tool Lost (taken from the route, Amendment 10) and extend INV-LOST-11: a route toolId that is not the loan's tool is refused loan-not-found (conformance 2026-11-01, finding 1) — v2: declared on the command and in the model; INV-LOST-11 extended, with a scenario (2026-11-01)

Slice: Close Account

Intent

Let a neighbor who is moving away or no longer wants to take part close their own account, from My Account. Closing is the neighbor's own choice, and it is final: nothing reopens, suspends or reinstates a closed account. A neighbor who wants to come back signs up again as a new account.

Closing records Neighbor Account Closed and, for each of the neighbor's holds, Hold Cancelled; what follows is decided by the views and slices that read them:

  • All of the neighbor's holds end, each by its Hold Cancelled. Holds waiting behind theirs move up, and a tool set aside for them passes to the next hold, or becomes available if none is waiting, as when a set-aside expires (My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Tool Catalog).
  • The neighbor can still view My Account, read-only, and can't borrow, extend or place holds (My Account, Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold).
  • A closed account is never flagged. The Neighbors screen shows it as closed, with no action and no open flags (Neighbors To Flag, Neighbors).
  • If the account was suspended when it was closed, its email can't be used to sign up again (Register Neighbor, INV-REG-4). Otherwise it can.

Trigger & Actor

The neighbor, from the My Account screen, on their own active or suspended account. My Account offers Close Account on any account that isn't closed. While the neighbor has a tool on loan, the closing is refused with a reason they can see (INV-CLS-7). The shed manager doesn't close accounts. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID. It resolves a person to their newest account, and to a closed one only when there is no newer.

Command / Input

Command: Close Account

A NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The account to close: the acting neighbor's own, who must be the one making the request (INV-CLS-1). Must be a registered account (INV-CLS-8).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Account @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Account Closed → context Neighbors Read by: My Account and Neighbors (the account shows as closed), and Neighbors To Flag (the late-return count ends).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
whileSuspended Bool yes Set by the system: yes if the account was suspended when it was closed (Neighbor Suspended with no Neighbor Reinstated since). Register Neighbor reads it to keep that email from being used again (INV-CLS-9).
closedAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices, as any cancellation (the hold ends).

The same event Cancel Hold records, recorded here once per hold the neighbor has, waiting or set aside, in the same decision as Neighbor Account Closed. The decider reads the holds it ends. With no such hold, none is recorded; the readers can't tell these from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes Set by the system: the hold being ended, from its Hold Placed.
cancelledAt Instant yes Set by the system: the same moment as Neighbor Account Closed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Account Closed changes the account's entry in My Account and Neighbors; the Hold Cancelled recorded with it end the neighbor's holds in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CLS-1: A neighbor closes their own account themselves.
    • The command names the account in neighborId, and the request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch otherwise). The shed manager doesn't close accounts.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-CLS-2: An active or a suspended account can be closed.
    • Closing an account that is already closed succeeds and records nothing new, so a double submit or a retry never fails and never records a second Neighbor Account Closed.
  • INV-CLS-7: An account can't be closed while the neighbor has any tool on loan, overdue or not.
    • A loan is on loan from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for it. A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost no longer counts.
    • So a closed account never has a tool out.
  • INV-CLS-8: The account must exist.
  • INV-CLS-9: Neighbor Account Closed records whether the account was suspended when it was closed.
    • Suspended means Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana is registered as N1, is active, and has no tools on loan.

  • Happy path (INV-CLS-2, INV-CLS-9)
    • Given: Ana has a hold waiting on the cordless drill, at position 1
    • When: Ana closes her account from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1, with whileSuspended no, and Hold Cancelled for her hold on the drill.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-CLS-2, INV-CLS-9)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, with no holds
    • When: Ana closes her account
    • Then: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1, with whileSuspended yes, and nothing else.
  • Reinstated neighbor closes their account (INV-CLS-9)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has since been reinstated
    • When: Ana closes her account
    • Then: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1, with whileSuspended no.
  • Closing while a tool is set aside (INV-CLS-2)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ana, and Cara's hold is waiting
    • When: Ana closes her account
    • Then: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1, and Hold Cancelled for her set-aside hold. A set-aside is not a loan, so it doesn't stop the closing; the drill passes to Cara's hold.
  • Closing with a tool still on loan (INV-CLS-7)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, not overdue
    • When: Ana tries to close her account
    • Then: refused with tools-on-loan: "Return all your tools before closing your account." No event is recorded.
  • Closing with an overdue tool (INV-CLS-7)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, and it is overdue
    • When: Ana tries to close her account
    • Then: refused with tools-on-loan. No event is recorded.
  • Closing after a tool was recorded lost (INV-CLS-7)
    • Given: Ana's only loan, of the hedge trimmer, ended when the shed manager recorded it lost
    • When: Ana closes her account
    • Then: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1.
  • Closing after returning everything (INV-CLS-7)
    • Given: Ana had the ladder on loan and has since returned it
    • When: Ana closes her account
    • Then: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1.
  • Closing twice (INV-CLS-2)
    • Given: Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for N1
    • When: Ana closes her account again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Someone else's account (INV-CLS-1)
    • Given: N1 is Ana's account
    • When: a request to close N1 comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only close your own account." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown account (INV-CLS-8)
    • Given: no account N9 has been registered
    • When: a request to close N9 arrives
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-CLS-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to close an account
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the My Account screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then requester-mismatch (INV-CLS-1).
  2. neighbor-not-found (INV-CLS-8).
  3. If the account is already closed, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-CLS-2).
  4. tools-on-loan (INV-CLS-7).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-CLS-1
requester-mismatch You can only close your own account. INV-CLS-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CLS-8
tools-on-loan Return all your tools before closing your account. INV-CLS-7

requester-mismatch and neighbor-not-found mean the same conditions as in the other neighbor commands. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: closing an account that is already closed succeeds and records nothing (INV-CLS-2).

Requests at the same moment: Close Account is decided against the neighbor's loans and status as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. If a checkout for the neighbor is decided just before the closing, the closing is refused with tools-on-loan. If a suspension or reinstatement is decided just before, whileSuspended reflects it.

There are no external calls in this slice, and no email is sent.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the neighbor may close their own account (INV-CLS-1). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Account Closed holds only the account ID, whether it was suspended, and a time. Closing doesn't erase the neighbor's name or email: they are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (this slice): neighborId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs. whileSuspended is new on Neighbor Account Closed; readers that need only {neighborId} are unaffected, and Register Neighbor can read it instead of working out the status itself.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Account, Neighbors and Neighbors To Flag (Neighbor Account Closed); My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire and Pickup Notices To Send (the Hold Cancelled recorded here). Register Neighbor reads whileSuspended for INV-REG-4. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Suspend Neighbor, Reinstate Neighbor and Change Email refuse a closed account.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded to Neighbors (2026-11-01)
